bull_bear.body: Debt expansion: working capital limit increasing by ₹50 Cr to ₹300 Cr; no equity dilution planned; capex focused on galvanization plant; no dividend policy mentioned; reinvestment in capacity and export readiness
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution delays in EPC projects; raw material price volatility; currency risk on exports; regulatory delays in international approvals (e.g., USA/Canada); competition from Valmont and Skipper; dependence on government tenders
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, optimistic, and detail-oriented; strong emphasis on execution capability, margin sustainability, and technological edge; proactive on export and monopole opportunity; transparent on order book and capex; avoids overpromising on railway order capture
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Rural electrification order of ₹750 Cr is localized near manufacturing units, reducing logistics cost and improving margins; monopole plant is not just capacity expansion but a product differentiation play with no direct Indian competitor; Ramboll design IP provides structural cost advantage not easily replicable
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- integration: In-house hot-dip galvanising alongside fabrication gives control over coating quality and durability — evidence: 'With hot-dip galvanising carried out within our own facilities, we maintain greater control over coating quality and durability'
- scale: Long operating track record in telecom tower manufacturing — evidence: 'Having supplied more than 50,000 telecom towers'
- technology: In-house design collaboration with Ramboll for optimised tower/monopole engineering — evidence: 'Optimised tower and monopole designs through in-house capabilities and collaboration with Ramboll'
- licence/regulatory: RDSO approval broadens eligibility for railway/heavy steel structure contracts — evidence: 'The Company is an RDSO-approved manufacturer of heavy steel structures'
- integration: EMC acquisition adds substation/transmission EPC capability (switchgear, protection systems, commissioning) that would otherwise take years to build organically — evidence: 'EMC brought us execution capacity and specialised machinery configured for power system and substation applications ... had we built that competence organically it would have taken years'
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw-material price volatility — Steel, zinc, fuel and freight cost volatility can affect procurement costs and project margins, particularly on long-duration, fixed-price EPC contracts.
- Project execution and working-capital risk — Delays in approvals, site access, land availability, material movement, customer payments or contractual milestones can affect project schedules, receivable cycles and profitability given the Company's complex EPC and infrastructure assignments.
- Regulatory and policy dependence — Business is affected by changes in government policy, regulatory requirements and infrastructure spending across power, telecom, railways and renewable energy.
- Quality, supply-chain and manpower constraints — Timely availability of material, skilled technical personnel and logistics support remain relevant risks to execution.
- EMC integration risk — The integration of EMC Limited presents significant opportunity while requiring effective alignment of people, processes, systems and governance practices across the enlarged Group.
- Customer credit and receivables risk — The Company applies expected credit loss assessment and periodic review of collection and retention-money positions, reflecting exposure to project receivables and customer payment risk.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Salasar Techno Engineering designs, fabricates, galvanises and executes engineered steel structures and EPC solutions for telecom, power transmission, railway electrification, renewable energy, smart cities and heavy/complex steel structures, serving telecom operators, power-sector organisations, EPC service providers, infrastructure companies and government organisations. It combines in-house engineering and manufacturing with EPC execution capability, including substation and transmission EPC through its subsidiary EMC Limited.

outlook.body: EBITDA margins sustain 9-10%; revenue growth driven by order book execution and new galvanization plant; expects additional ₹50 Cr revenue from new plant in FY24; targets export expansion and railway electrification orders.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: ₹1,435 Cr total: ₹1,243 Cr EPC; ₹88 Cr Towers & Poles; ₹100 Cr Heavy Steel Structures; ₹400 Cr Railway Electrification (under execution); ₹750 Cr Rural Electrification (under execution)
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: New galvanization plant enables monopole production for 400kV+ transmission lines; export potential to USA/Canada; rural electrification pipeline of ₹25,000 Cr; 5G tower demand doubling; railway capex of ₹1.07 Lakh Cr; monopole segment has low competition
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Deepen presence in sectors already understood (power transmission, railways, telecom, renewable energy, poles, heavy steel structures) while selectively entering adjacent segments where capability gives genuine advantage.
- Pursue growth selectively, favouring projects aligned to capabilities and offering sustainable returns over those that simply add revenue.
- Build towards being recognised as an integrated infrastructure partner across the value chain — engineering, design, fabrication, galvanising, supply, erection and commissioning — rather than a manufacturer or a contractor alone.
- Measured, selective approach to international expansion, building a track record project by project.
- Disciplined order acquisition going forward, with greater emphasis on project quality, sustainable returns and efficient conversion of the order book into revenue.
- Improve capacity utilisation and productivity before adding new capacity.
- Focus on tighter tolerances, shorter cycle times, fewer defects and faster response to changing project requirements as the basis of competitive execution.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26 the reporting boundary expanded to include the new Bhilai-Chhattisgarh manufacturing unit and the new Noida Corporate Office. The Company continued to strengthen production capabilities across towers, monopoles, utility structures, poles and heavy steel structures, and continues to focus on improving capacity utilisation, productivity and throughput before adding further capacity. Substation mandates at Thirubuvanai, Thavalakuppam and Lawspet followed from the integration of EMC Limited's execution capacity for power-system and substation applications.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India is entering a sustained infrastructure investment cycle driven by government capital expenditure, policy support and rising demand for power, digital connectivity, modern railways and industrial infrastructure.
- Railway electrification opportunity is transitioning from mass electrification of the legacy network to electrification of new lines, capacity augmentation and system modernisation, with 99.6% of the broad-gauge network electrified by March 2026.
- Renewable-energy demand is expected to remain strong, led by solar, supporting demand for module mounting structures, galvanised steel components and transmission infrastructure.
- Heavy steel structure demand is closely linked to India's broader capital-expenditure cycle and the shift towards prefabricated, faster and more durable construction systems.
- The Poles segment witnessed strong demand during the year, supported by requirements across power, telecom, urban infrastructure and utility applications.
- The EPC business remained an important growth platform, supported by opportunities in power transmission, railway infrastructure and other large-scale infrastructure projects.
- Diversified presence across multiple infrastructure segments provides resilience by reducing dependence on any single segment.
- Raw-material price volatility (steel, zinc, copper, aluminium, fuel, freight) is a margin risk, particularly on fixed-price contracts.
- The Company closed the year with an order book of approximately `2,160 crore, compared with `2,155 crore in the previous year.
- Secured EPC orders aggregating approximately `300 crore from customers including Himachal Infracon, PGCIL, RRVPNL, UPPTCL and North Western Railway, among others.
- Secured a Heavy Steel Structure order of approximately `74 crore from the Adani Group, along with significant orders for the supply of poles.
- Order book diversity spans EPC, power transmission, railways, heavy steel structures, poles, manufacturing and exports, providing a balanced foundation for future execution and revenue visibility.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Salasar Techno Engineering is a vertically integrated infrastructure player with dominant positioning in telecom towers and power EPC, benefiting from India's massive grid modernization and 5G rollout. The upcoming Asia's largest galvanization plant will unlock high-margin monopole production, enhancing revenue visibility and margins.

open.item: The Poles segment is expected to remain a key focus and the EPC division should register healthy growth as orders in hand are executed faster.
Integrate EMC's engineering standards, project management and procurement systems across the combined order book to unlock the full value of the merger.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India is entering a sustained infrastructure investment cycle driven by government capital expenditure, policy support and rising demand for power, digital connectivity, modern railways and industrial infrastructure.
- Railway electrification opportunity is transitioning from mass electrification of the legacy network to electrification of new lines, capacity augmentation and system modernisation, with 99.6% of the broad-gauge network electrified by March 2026.
- Renewable-energy demand is expected to remain strong, led by solar, supporting demand for module mounting structures, galvanised steel components and transmission infrastructure.
- Heavy steel structure demand is closely linked to India's broader capital-expenditure cycle and the shift towards prefabricated, faster and more durable construction systems.
- The Poles segment witnessed strong demand during the year, supported by requirements across power, telecom, urban infrastructure and utility applications.
- The EPC business remained an important growth platform, supported by opportunities in power transmission, railway infrastructure and other large-scale infrastructure projects.
- Diversified presence across multiple infrastructure segments provides resilience by reducing dependence on any single segment.
- Raw-material price volatility (steel, zinc, copper, aluminium, fuel, freight) is a margin risk, particularly on fixed-price contracts.
- The Company closed the year with an order book of approximately `2,160 crore, compared with `2,155 crore in the previous year.
- Secured EPC orders aggregating approximately `300 crore from customers including Himachal Infracon, PGCIL, RRVPNL, UPPTCL and North Western Railway, among others.
- Secured a Heavy Steel Structure order of approximately `74 crore from the Adani Group, along with significant orders for the supply of poles.
- Order book diversity spans EPC, power transmission, railways, heavy steel structures, poles, manufacturing and exports, providing a balanced foundation for future execution and revenue visibility.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin: 9.01% in Q1FY24 (up 99 bps YoY); sustainable range 9-10%; new galvanization plant expected to improve margins via vertical integration and premium monopole pricing; cost advantage from Ramboll designs reduces material cost by 40% vs conventional towers

capex_expansion.body: During FY 2025-26 the reporting boundary expanded to include the new Bhilai-Chhattisgarh manufacturing unit and the new Noida Corporate Office. The Company continued to strengthen production capabilities across towers, monopoles, utility structures, poles and heavy steel structures, and continues to focus on improving capacity utilisation, productivity and throughput before adding further capacity. Substation mandates at Thirubuvanai, Thavalakuppam and Lawspet followed from the integration of EMC Limited's execution capacity for power-system and substation applications.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, optimistic, and detail-oriented; strong emphasis on execution capability, margin sustainability, and technological edge; proactive on export and monopole opportunity; transparent on order book and capex; avoids overpromising on railway order capture

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- integration: In-house hot-dip galvanising alongside fabrication gives control over coating quality and durability — evidence: 'With hot-dip galvanising carried out within our own facilities, we maintain greater control over coating quality and durability'
- scale: Long operating track record in telecom tower manufacturing — evidence: 'Having supplied more than 50,000 telecom towers'
- technology: In-house design collaboration with Ramboll for optimised tower/monopole engineering — evidence: 'Optimised tower and monopole designs through in-house capabilities and collaboration with Ramboll'
- licence/regulatory: RDSO approval broadens eligibility for railway/heavy steel structure contracts — evidence: 'The Company is an RDSO-approved manufacturer of heavy steel structures'
- integration: EMC acquisition adds substation/transmission EPC capability (switchgear, protection systems, commissioning) that would otherwise take years to build organically — evidence: 'EMC brought us execution capacity and specialised machinery configured for power system and substation applications ... had we built that competence organically it would have taken years'

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Execution delays in EPC projects; raw material price volatility; currency risk on exports; regulatory delays in international approvals (e.g., USA/Canada); competition from Valmont and Skipper; dependence on government tenders

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Rural electrification order of ₹750 Cr is localized near manufacturing units, reducing logistics cost and improving margins; monopole plant is not just capacity expansion but a product differentiation play with no direct Indian competitor; Ramboll design IP provides structural cost advantage not easily replicable

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Deepen presence in sectors already understood (power transmission, railways, telecom, renewable energy, poles, heavy steel structures) while selectively entering adjacent segments where capability gives genuine advantage.
- Pursue growth selectively, favouring projects aligned to capabilities and offering sustainable returns over those that simply add revenue.
- Build towards being recognised as an integrated infrastructure partner across the value chain — engineering, design, fabrication, galvanising, supply, erection and commissioning — rather than a manufacturer or a contractor …

themes.title: Power transmission & renewable-evacuation capex
themes.need: Grid build-out to evacuate ~90 GW of new renewables is the broadest theme in the universe - pulling EHV/765kV transmission EPC, towers, conductors, OPGW, cables and HVDC. POWERGRID/ADANIENSOL TBCB pipeline plus state RDSS/underground-cabling capex (Rajesh Power 544291, OMPOWER) underpins multi-year visibility for EPC, tower (KP Green 544150, SKIPPER) and conductor/cable makers (KEI, RRKABEL, DYCL).
themes.driver: Fresh TBCB awards + execution ramp; EPC order inflows over next 1-2 quarters.

themes.title: Railway rolling-stock & component capex
themes.need: A ~INR2.65 lakh cr Railways capital outlay and a pending ~1-lakh-wagon tender ('anytime this year' per JWL) drive rolling-stock, wheelsets, springs, castings, bogie components and interiors - with deep import-substitution (Neetu Yoshi 544434 castings; Airfloa 544516 interiors; Concord 543619 electronics). TITAGARH/TEXRAIL/JWL lead wagons; RVNL/IRCON/GPTINFRA on rail EPC.
themes.driver: Indian Railways large wagon tender award (next 1-2 quarters); wheelset plant ramp; Vande Bharat / Kavach orders.

themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex
themes.need: 5G monetization, FTTH and tower/fibre densification drive the connectivity cycle - and Q1FY27 repriced the optical leg outright. STLTECH booked order intake of INR 13,100cr in ONE quarter, 1.7x its entire FY26 order book, anchored by a multi-year $1.1bn hyperscaler deal running through FY29, taking the open order book to INR 18,618cr (up 2.4x QoQ) on revenue of INR 1,910cr (+87%) and EBITDA INR 397cr (+184%). It then raised guidance twice on the same call - EBITDA margin target from 20%-by-end-FY27 (already hit at 20.8% in Q1) to 23%, and Data-Center + Enterprise mix from 30% to 50% of FY27 revenue, after DC went from 1% of revenue in FY26 to 21%. The catch is supply, not demand: ex the anchor deal quarterly intake fell to ~INR 3,000cr from INR 7,000-8,000cr because 'we have to pick and choose the orders basis the capacity availability', with germanium and helium named as binding raw-material constraints. BHARTIARTL on ARPU + 5G; INDUSTOWER on tower rollout; SUYOG-tier on passive infra; GTPL/HFCL-tier on broadband + fibre; tariff hikes and rural FTTH are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler ramp against germanium/helium supply constraints and the raised 23% margin / 50% DC-mix guides; tariff-hike flow-through; 5G/FTTH capex; tower tenancy adds.
